title: Are you monetizing your games?
author: estebansaa
selftext: or is more of a hobby thing?

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: I released a game a while ago but it only has 15 units sold. I marked the game as AI generated and I am not sure how much that affected sales. It could just be poor marketing

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: Yeah... I think it is just the typical gamedev experience. It is not easy to become profitable.

replies.author: EffortlessWriting
replies.body: Well yeah don't expect many sales if you're not marketing it.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I just share it in a few subs. I don't know much about effective marketing. Regardless, we live in a world where people constantly releases demos and games. That was before AI too. 

I hope my next release may see some success but we will see...

replies.author: yourfriendoz
replies.body: Did you ask AI to help you scaffold an effective guerilla marketing campaign!

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I asked AI for marketing advice and it told me not to pay for ads. 

AI feel less magically once you are looking for advice closer to monetization...

replies.author: yourfriendoz
replies.body:
Respectfully. I don't believe you asked AI for a marketing plan and it said "don't pay for ads... Full Stop."

That said, I wish you luck in your endeavors.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
well, it said a bunch of other things and offers recommendations obviously. I just didn't go into it. To be more specific, it pretty much said paid ads won't do much for someone in my position. 

I have seen other posts online saying AI transformed their marketing campaigns etc. I hope that happens to me eventually but no idea. Thanks though

replies.author: yourfriendoz
replies.body:
Respectfully. I don't believe you asked AI for a marketing plan and it said "don't pay for ads... Full Stop."

That said, I wish you luck in your endeavors.

replies.author: Appleslicer93
replies.body: Probably affected it severely. I didn't realize how insane the current cancel culture is for anything ai in game dev. Should get better in the coming years though

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I only promoted the game in this sub a couple other subs. I did get a few AI related comments but no idea. 

I also skipped demo/playtesting and that was a mistake in hindsight. The end result is actually somewhat boring. I am hoping to improve its value with content updates...

I think the game not finding its niche is worse but thats my 2 cents

comments.author: Disamble
comments.body: I’m just having fun seeing my words turned to fancy machine talk on AI studio lol really fun imo

comments.author: vurt72
comments.body:
Hobby.   
I do think there is a  small window where you can maybe sell if its really good (then no one will care if its AI or not).   
Eventually we will 100% get it to where we can have it make graphics AND code seamlessly, and then its over. it will be like trying to sell AI images or videos (which yes, you could do for a little while), why would anyone purchase something they can make themselves?

comments.author: Objective-Address810
comments.body:
I am aiming for monetization.

  
I have invested 6 months full time development into an RPG platform where humans can build RPG worlds on top of flexible systems, that AI will enhance.

There are no guarantees I can montetize it, but that is true of any product.

I have a long way to go for what I want to achieve, but one thing for sure no matter what I am learning heaps and having fun

replies.author: estebansaa
replies.body: what is your go to market and monetization plan?

replies.author: Objective-Address810
replies.body:
It’s still TBC, but only because we are focusing on the gameplay experience first.

We have some ideas, but still tweaking.
